executiveSummary: The developer reported Phase 3 complete on the production deployment, while the next frontend package remains prepared for reconciliation and release. The September 6 review clarified remaining responsibilities: client revisions, real workflow testing, launch-scope decisions and user training. The nexus-letter content was also sent for review. Development completion, production verification and client acceptance remain separate milestones; four to five weeks is a planning estimate rather than a committed launch date.

work.title: Nexus-letter content submitted for review
work.detail: Content from the supplied documents was added to the private nexus-letter page and sent to the client. The same email asked for confirmation of the portal’s sender domain before DNS setup. It did not confirm successful email sending.
work.whyItMatters: Moves content to review and identifies the specific email configuration decision.

work.title: Phase 3 reported complete on the development side
work.detail: The developer reported Phase 3 built, tested and live on the production deployment. The proposed walkthrough remains the next acceptance step; this report does not independently certify every production workflow.
work.whyItMatters: Provides the reported milestone against which the walkthrough and remaining work will be assessed.

work.title: Prepared frontend package and release boundary reviewed
work.detail: The September 6 code and responsibility review identified prepared documents, editable settings, archive access, session-refresh and accessibility work in PR 5. The package still needed reconciliation with the developer’s latest work and release review; it was not merged or deployed in that evidence.
work.whyItMatters: Distinguishes already-built frontend work from the steps needed to make it part of the accepted release.

work.title: Workflow, ownership and acceptance checklist prepared
work.detail: The original agreement, roadmap and current code were reconciled into a remaining-work checklist covering lifecycle events, Payment Watch, documents, settings, mobile behavior and the claimant-portal launch boundary. The checklist also separates frontend work from backend and client-decision dependencies.
work.whyItMatters: Gives the walkthrough a concrete decision and test list rather than treating a development claim as acceptance.

work.title: Training and next-phase plan defined
work.detail: The plan calls for refreshing user guides against final screens, completing screenshots and walkthrough materials, organizing remaining tasks with owners, and recording the client’s launch decisions. Prepared documentation is not completed training.
work.whyItMatters: Makes the handoff requirements visible before final testing and go-live.

decisions.decision: Hold a Phase 3 walkthrough the following week before starting Phase 4.

nextSteps.title: Phase 3 walkthrough
nextSteps.detail: Walk the client through Phase 3 before Phase 4 begins; this is the acceptance gate that development completion does not by itself satisfy.

nextSteps.title: Client review of the nexus letter page
nextSteps.detail: The nexus letters page content was sent for client review on September 3; the review response is the open dependency.

nextSteps.title: Run full workflow testing
nextSteps.detail: Payment Watch, documents, settings and mobile checks, after reconciling with the developer's latest changes and finishing client revisions.

nextSteps.title: Finish user guides and walkthrough materials
nextSteps.detail: Required before the walkthrough can close the open launch-scope decisions.

nextSteps.title: Confirm launch feature scope, then lock final testing and go-live dates
nextSteps.detail: The walkthrough is the decision gate; dates are explicitly not locked until it happens. Roughly four to five weeks remains a working estimate.

caveats: Phase 3 completion is developer-reported; client acceptance and authenticated production workflow checks are not established by that claim.
The September 6 review found PR 5 prepared but not merged or deployed. Later release status requires a fresh check.
The four-to-five-week estimate is not a committed launch date.
The private nexus-letter page is a content-review deliverable, separate from the software release.
headline: Make the next release reviewable.
summaryFollow: The actions below separate verified changes, reported progress and work awaiting review.
coverNote: The work. The results. What comes next.
